# Brief for the coach: Monday incline curl added, program now on its fourth version

## What was done and why

Joe's direct biceps work was all on one day: Sunday's deadlift and legs session carries dumbbell bicep curls, 3 sets of 8–12 at RPE 8, and dumbbell hammer curls, 3 sets of 10–12 at RPE 8. Six direct sets, all in one session. Monday's OHP, back and arms session was the lightest lifting day with only four exercises. The program he ran before this engine had incline curls on both of its pull days, and his profile says direct biceps work should be dumbbell curls, not barbell.

So I added **Incline Curl (Dumbbell), 3 sets of 8–12 reps at RPE 8, 75 seconds rest**, as the last exercise of Monday. Progression is double progression: once every set reaches 12 reps, the load goes up. Cues recorded for it: bench at about 45 degrees, arms hanging straight down behind the torso, elbows stay back with a full stretch at the bottom, no shoulder swing. No start load was set for it, so the next weekly plan will derive the opening weight from his past incline curl logs; if you'd rather set it by hand, say so before the week is drafted.

Direct biceps work goes from 6 sets in one session to 9 sets across two days.

The reason recorded on the program reads: direct biceps work was six sets in one session; an incline curl on Monday makes it nine over two days, at long muscle length, and keeps the lightest lifting day inside its cap.

## Monday as it now stands

1. Overhead Press (Barbell): warm-ups of 1×5 and 1×3, then a top set of 5 at RPE 8, then 4 back-off sets of 6 at 85 % of the top set. 180 s rest.
2. Chest Supported Row (Dumbbell): 4 sets of 8–12 at RPE 8. 120 s rest.
3. Lateral Raise (Dumbbell): 3 sets of 12–15 at RPE 8, 60 s rest, supersetted with
4. Rear Delt Fly (Dumbbell): 3 sets of 12–15 at RPE 8, 60 s rest.
5. Incline Curl (Dumbbell): 3 sets of 8–12 at RPE 8. 75 s rest. **New.**

The kettlebell swing EMOM still sits beside it on Monday as its own conditioning session.

## What the engine recorded

- The program is now on its **fourth version**, an amendment (not a redesign), adopted 4 November 2026. Emphasis stays hypertrophy, location home.
- The only difference from the third version is the one added line on Monday. Nothing else moved; no sessions added or removed.
- The rotation stays at week A. The training block that opened on **1 November 2026 continues**; it was not reset, so the fatigue and deload clock keeps running from that date.
- Session time estimates against their caps, with the curl included: Monday **53 of 75 minutes**, Wednesday 39 of 75, Friday 65 of 75, Saturday 65 of 90, Sunday 65 of 90. Everything is inside cap.
- Start loads the engine will push to Hevy, in his units and in Hevy's kilograms: Farmers Walk (Dumbbell) on Sunday 50 lb (45.3592 kg); Kettlebell Swing 40 lb (18.1437 kg) in both the swing EMOM and the strength circuit. These were already in the program; nothing new there.
- The export and the pages were republished and committed.

## The flags, what they mean, and what clears each

**Three Hevy routines have drifted from the approved plan.** The weekly plan approved on 2 November 2026 says one thing; Joe's copies of three routines in Hevy now say another. Specifically:

- One routine differs in the duration of the second set of its first exercise.
- One differs in the reps of sets 5, 6 and 7 of its first exercise, and in the weight of sets 1, 2 and 3 of its second exercise.
- One differs in the weight of sets 1 through 4 of its third exercise, the durations of sets 1 and 2 of its fourth exercise, and the weight of sets 1 through 3 of its sixth exercise.

This is not caused by today's change; it is the state of Hevy. What it means for training: his phone is showing numbers the plan didn't prescribe, most likely because he edited them mid-session. What clears it: either the next weekly plan carries an override that adopts his edits as the plan, or the next push to Hevy overwrites his edits with the plan. **Joe needs to say which he wants** before the next week is pushed, otherwise his hand changes are lost.

**Deadlift weekly dose is below the band.** The program targets 4 hard deadlift sets a week; the engine's band for a maintenance phase is 5–15. This is a known and accepted position carried forward from the previous version, with the reason: Sunday plans exactly four hard sets, the top set and three back-offs; Friday's Romanian deadlift carries the hinge pattern; the PT sometimes adds deadlifts on Tuesday; a target of 5 would show as under-target every week the session is done as written. Nothing to change unless you want Sunday to grow a fourth back-off.

**Friday's strict pull-up single doesn't match a hypertrophy emphasis.** One rep at RPE 10 is a test, not volume. Also accepted and carried forward: the strict single is the weekly measure while his max is 1; the negatives and band pull-ups do the building under their own progressions; the strict line turns into real working sets once the test rep passes about five.

## What Joe must agree to

The change is recorded in the program, but **his Hevy routines have not been touched**. Hevy only changes when the next weekly plan is drafted and approved for pushing. At that point he'll be shown Monday with the incline curl added and asked to confirm. That same approval is where the three drifted routines get settled, so ask him now whether those mid-session edits were deliberate and should become the plan, or were one-offs he's happy to lose.

**Conditioning placement**

Keep the kettlebell swing session on Monday, where it already sits, and put the strength circuit on Thursday.

Here's the reasoning, day by day:

- **Monday, swings.** It's your lightest lifting day (about 53 minutes of a 75 minute slot), so there's room, and it's an upper-body day so the swings don't compete with heavy legs. Yes, it's the day after Sunday's deadlift, but the swings are light and brisk, and that kind of easy hinge work the day after a heavy one tends to help you loosen up rather than dig the hole deeper. If a Monday ever comes when your lower back feels beaten up from Sunday, skip the swings that week rather than grind through them.
- **Thursday, circuit.** It's your only empty day. The circuit is full-body (goblet squat, ring push-up, swing, mountain climber) and would land on tired muscles anywhere else: Wednesday already has the pull-up work plus your lunchtime run, Friday is squats, Saturday is bench and dips, Sunday is deadlifts and a run. Thursday gives you a day between the Wednesday run and the circuit, and a day between the circuit and Friday squats. Keep the circuit honest but not brutal, so Friday's squats aren't paying for it.

If you'd rather keep Thursday as a true day off, the fallback for the circuit is Saturday after bench. Saturday has the most spare time (about 65 of 90 minutes), and the circuit's push-ups come after you've already pressed, which costs nothing. Don't put it on Friday or Sunday; those are the heaviest leg days and the circuit's squats and swings would interfere.

**Two things to settle before next week's plan goes to your phone**

1. Three of your routines in the app currently carry edits you made during sessions: a changed hold time on one, different reps and weights on another, and weight and duration changes on a third. When next week's plan is pushed, those edits will either be kept as the new plan or overwritten with what was prescribed. Were they deliberate changes you want to keep, or one-offs you're happy to lose?
2. The Monday incline curl has no opening weight set yet. The plan will pick one from your past incline curl logs unless you'd rather name a weight yourself.
